description.narrative: This nine-month plan aims to strengthen the organisation's capacity by integrating and coordinating communications to achieve programmatic goals. We will identify opportunities both internally and externally to raise awareness of our work, provide communication support to promote the Commonwealth’s efforts on global platforms, and showcase the uniqueness, relevance, and impact of our work to audiences. Additionally, we will regularly review internal and external communications to guide our efforts and reinforce the Commonwealth brand. The Communications Division will develop strategies and tactics to connect the Commonwealth Secretariat's work to global audiences. The Communications team will identify the best channels for message distribution to achieve communication objectives. They will plan and consider different audiences, tailoring key messages to each group, publish high-quality content to attract diverse audiences, utilise mainstream media, online media, social media, and intranet to share stories about the Commonwealth, ensure consistent branding of Commonwealth content across all channels—impactful publications will help maintain trust—and use social media and multimedia to enhance the brand. An improved website with quality content and functionality will drive traffic to all digital channels. Effective campaigns, major events, and outreach activities will showcase the work of the Commonwealth, raise awareness, and encourage action. Better access to printed publications and knowledge resources will increase visibility. The team will also prepare and support spokespeople for interviews across various platforms, including television, radio, and social media. The 2026/27 budget year will include activities and deliverables carried over from last year, along with new public outreach efforts for the upcoming year that align with our Communication Strategy. CHOGM in Antigua and Barbuda provides an opportunity to enhance and promote the Commonwealth's reputation worldwide. The communications team will manage journalists' accreditation and organise the journalists' pool, creating high-quality content such as photos and videos to showcase the work of the Commonwealth across the four pillars of the Strategic Plan. Digital and social media will be essential for CHOGM by offering live updates—sharing key takeaways, social media graphics, quotes, and moments in real time; encouraging engagement where attendees can share thoughts and retweet event outcomes; expanding reach by broadcasting key messages to a global audience; and using hashtag campaigns to monitor conversations. Digital content creation and sharing will be crucial for producing shareable content, including engaging posts, videos, and infographics that highlight the key theme and showcase thought leadership in specific thematic or program areas. Public relations efforts will generate buzz before, during, and after CHOGM, including sharing themes, interviews, stories, sessions, press releases, photos, highlights of key moments, outcomes, quotes, and next steps. The Envoy Programme and CHOGM Fundraising are initiatives designed to improve brand perception by (1) building credibility through partnerships with respected individuals and organisations, (2) demonstrating Comsec's responsibility by showing its commitment to the cause, (3) increasing engagement by encouraging support for a worthy cause, (4) generating content by creating shareable, high-quality material around the Envoy programme and CHOGM fundraising activities, and (5) ensuring transparency by sharing the impact and results of these efforts.
